findings.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError (nil['id']) when no site_settings row exists for 'embed_category', breaking db:migrate for most existing installs
Migration builds SQL by directly interpolating the legacy embeddable_hosts setting value into an INSERT statement, allowing SQL injection or migration crashes on values containing a single quote
record_for_host compares lower(host) against a non-downcased host bind variable, so case-insensitive host matching silently fails for mixed/upper-case hostnames
before_validation calls host.sub! unconditionally, raising NoMethodError instead of a validation error when host is nil/blank
Controller update and destroy actions fetch the host via .where(id: params[:id]).first without a nil check, causing NoMethodError (500) instead of a proper 404 for nonexistent ids
type.replace('_', '-') in rest.js.es6 only replaces the first underscore, misrouting admin model types with more than one underscore
embeddable_hosts.host column has no index despite being looked up on every embed request, and lookups use lower(host) which wouldn't use a plain btree index anyway
Controller specs for embeddable_hosts_controller and embedding_controller only check the AdminController subclass, with no coverage of create/update/destroy or the nil-host 500 paths

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration builds SQL by directly interpolating the legacy embeddable_hosts setting value into an INSERT statement, allowing SQL injection or migration crashes on values containing a single quote

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration reads the legacy site setting value `embeddable_hosts`, splits it into lines, and then executes raw SQL with direct string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. If any host line contains a single quote (or other SQL-special characters), the SQL becomes invalid and the migration can crash; because it’s unescaped interpolation, it also creates an SQL injection vector in the migration context (the value ultimately originates from an admin-configurable setting stored in DB). A safer approach would be using `quote(h)` / bind params / ActiveRecord insert APIs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: type.replace('_', '-') in rest.js.es6 only replaces the first underscore, misrouting admin model types with more than one underscore

adjudication.rationale: In `rest.js.es6`, `basePath(store, type)` now checks `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-')) !== -1`. While it’s true that JS `String#replace` without a global regex only replaces the first underscore, the admin model types involved in this diff (`embeddable_host`, `site_customization`) each contain only a single underscore, so they are correctly transformed to `embeddable-host` / `site-customization`. The proposed issue would only manifest for a type with 2+ underscores, which is not introduced or exercised by this diff, so it’s not a verifiable defect here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable_hosts.host column has no index despite being looked up on every embed request, and lookups use lower(host) which wouldn't use a plain btree index anyway

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an `embeddable_hosts` table (migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`) with columns `host` and `category_id` but no index on `host`. Runtime checks call `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` on embed-related requests (`EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`), and that method performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`. Without an index this is a table scan, and even adding a plain btree index on `host` would not be used by `lower(host)` in Postgres unless an expression index (e.g., `index on lower(host)`) or normalized storage is used. This is a real, verifiable performance issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs for embeddable_hosts_controller and embedding_controller only check the AdminController subclass, with no coverage of create/update/destroy or the nil-host 500 paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new controller specs (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) that only assert each controller is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. The new controllers themselves implement behaviorful actions (EmbeddableHostsController#create/update/destroy and EmbeddingController#show/update) including cases where records may be nil (e.g., update/destroy look up by id and then call save_host/destroy). None of those action paths are exercised by the added specs, so the finding about lack of meaningful coverage is directly verifiable from the diff.
